# HEVC compressed-reference memory audit

**AI disclosure:** This file, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI.

Offline research for [omarchy-m1-video#77](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/77).
It extracts `calc_tile_meta` / `fill_comp` / `mv_color_size` from pinned Asahi
AVD, reproduces the published 448×240 layouts, and explains VA vs Gst tail
placement. Parent [libva-v4l2_request#42](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/42)
stays open. No hardware, module, or shipped patch.

## Run

```
python3 experiments/hevc-reference-memory/tests.py
```

Picture 28 / POC32 public records: both clients share `comp_start=161280`,
`comp_size=177152`, offsets `[114688,0,176128,118784]`, `mv_size=7168`.
Gst MMAP `length=345600` / `mv_offset=338432`. VA DMABUF `length=368128` /
`mv_offset=360960`. The driver programs MV at `plane_length - mv_size`
(`avd-hevc.c:1281`). Gst length equals packed `sizeimage`, so MV follows
compressed data. VA's importer allocated more; the extra 22528 bytes sit
between compressed data and MV. That is **not a proved bug**.

A `-DTILE_Y=16` rebuild of the extracted `fill_comp` misses the published
offsets (required mutation).

See [OWNERSHIP.md](OWNERSHIP.md) and [next-observation.md](next-observation.md).
Firmware-written compressed bytes remain unknown. This ticket does not
authorize a capture of those bytes.
